title: Dispatch: Non-Dolt checkpoint restore proof for revokedPosition (review 5 evidence R4)
description:
Bounded follow-up to eshyra-jhpt.rev11 (merged at f468462). External review #5118796759 evidence item R4 requires: "Checkpoint restore followed by the normal .2 read/list API reproduces the same revocation position". rev11 added that assertion ONLY inside `describe.skipIf(!doltOk)('CheckpointStore.restoreToNewWorkingCopy')` in packages/core/test/checkpoint.restore.test.ts. Dolt is absent on this machine AND in CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml never installs it), so that evidence has never executed anywhere. A test that never runs is a claim, not evidence.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev12 on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev12, cut from eshyra-jhpt at f468462. npm ci already run.

THE FIX
`materialize(records, destDbPath)` in packages/core/src/persistence/checkpoint/store.ts rebuilds a SQLite database from SnapshotRecord[] (schema + rows) with NO Dolt involvement — it is exactly the restore step, and only the record source (Dolt) is gated. Make the SQLite half of restore testable without Dolt:
1. Export `materialize` from store.ts under a clear name (e.g. `materializeSnapshot`) and re-export it from packages/core/src/internal.ts ONLY (no root-export change). Keep its behaviour byte-for-byte identical; do not change CheckpointStore.
2. In the NON-gated `describe('checkpoint serialization')` block of checkpoint.restore.test.ts, add a test that: builds an in-memory campaign with a created rule, a superseded chain, and a rule revoked at a canonical __future__ position (mirror the fixture the gated test already uses); calls serializeCampaign(db); calls materializeSnapshot(records, <tmp file under a mkdtemp dir>); opens the restored file with openDatabase; and asserts via getCampaignRule AND listCampaignRules (typed .2 APIs, no SQL) that status, supersededBy, effectivePosition and revokedPosition all equal the pre-checkpoint typed reads (deep-equal the whole CampaignRule objects). Also assert listActiveCampaignRulesAtPosition agrees on the restored DB at a position before and after the revocation. Clean the temp dir in finally.
3. Leave the Dolt-gated assertion in place (it still runs wherever Dolt exists).

NEGATIVE PROOF: the new test must FAIL if rowToRule stops hydrating revokedPosition — demonstrate by temporarily reverting that hydration (or stubbing) and observing the failure, then restore; report the observed failure message. It cannot fail "against f468462" as such because the production code is already correct; the proof is that the assertion is live.

Do NOT change anything else. VERIFICATION: npm run verify:worktree BEFORE committing; report pass/skip counts and confirm worktree-local resolution.
